objective: Show and remove the compact section menu without losing the relationship to the rightmost hamburger trigger or trapping keyboard focus.
spatial_relationship: The menu appears six pixels below its final position directly beneath the rightmost trigger and exits toward that trigger.

selection_rationale.escalation_reason: The menu must animate while React removes it from the DOM, so AnimatePresence supplies the unmount lifecycle that a plain CSS transition cannot own reliably.

rejected_alternatives.why_not: Pointer users benefit from a brief relationship cue between the trigger and the detached menu surface.
React unmounts the closed menu, so an authored exit transition would need additional retained-state lifecycle code.
Imperative animation and cancellation would duplicate lifecycle behavior already provided by AnimatePresence.

sequence.change: pointer path: opacity 0 to 1 and translateY -6px to 0px; keyboard path: instant final state

timing.derivation: The surface travels only six pixels and responds to a direct control, so it must complete well below 300ms and never delay the committed menu state.

easing.character: Fast and precise with no bounce, preserving the menu's utilitarian reading behavior.

interruption.notes: A single keyed AnimatePresence child owns the current menu surface and retargets on repeated pointer toggles.

responsive.mobile: The panel width is capped to the viewport and travel remains six pixels.
responsive.tablet: The panel remains right aligned below the trigger.
responsive.desktop: The panel remains right aligned below the trigger.
responsive.orientation_or_input_notes: Keyboard activation suppresses motion and moves focus to the first menu link; pointer activation leaves focus on the trigger.

reduced_motion.implementation: MotionConfig reducedMotion user and the menuMotion guard set the transition duration to one millisecond.
reduced_motion.vestibular_review: Only a six-pixel local translation exists; reduced motion and keyboard activation remove it completely.

keyboard_and_focus.focus_behavior: Keyboard open focuses the first section link; Escape closes the menu and returns visible focus to the hamburger trigger.

ssr.hydration_notes: The standalone Vite site is client-rendered; the menu is closed in the initial render and therefore has no pre-animation flash.

cleanup.on_unmount: AnimatePresence and Motion cancel the active menu animation when the component unmounts.
cleanup.listeners_and_observers: The effect registers Escape and outside-pointer listeners only while open, then removes both in the useEffect cleanup.
cleanup.route_change_notes: The standalone site has no client routes; section-link activation closes the menu before native anchor navigation.

performance_budget.cls_contribution: None because the panel is absolutely positioned outside document flow.
performance_budget.inp_notes: React state commits before the animation; no measurement or awaited work runs in the click handler.
performance_budget.notes: The menu reuses the existing Framer dependency and animates only one small compositor layer.

acceptance_criteria: The hamburger is the rightmost control at every tested viewport.
Pointer open and close complete within 180 milliseconds without a visual jump.
Keyboard open is instant and places focus on the first section link.
Escape closes the menu and returns focus to the hamburger button.
Ten rapid toggles leave exactly one correct open or closed state.
expected_failure_modes: Focus remains on a removed menu link after Escape.
Rapid toggles create duplicate menu panels.
The right-aligned panel causes horizontal overflow at 320 pixels.
